nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni-Mo hydroxide growth
nodes.procedure: The molybdenum precursor 20 mM of (NH₃)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O was dissolved in 35 mL of distilled water and stirred for 30 min to prepare a transparent solution. The NF was annealed at 400 °C for 1 h under an Ar atmosphere to promote the adsorption of the Mo precursors during hydrothermal synthesis. The prepared solution was then transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, and the annealed NF was immersed in the solution. The autoclave was sealed, heated at 180 °C for 12 h in an oven, and then cooled to room temperature (25 °C). When the hydrothermal reaction was complete, the obtained Ni–Mo hydroxide on the NF was washed several times with distilled water to eliminate the solution and excess precursor. Finally, it was dried overnight in an oven at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Ru drop-casting and phosphorization
nodes.procedure: 250 μL of 80 mM RuCl₃·xH₂O ethanol solution was uniformly dropped onto the obtained Ni–Mo hydroxide on NF and then dried at room temperature for 1 h. Thereafter, the treated Ni–Mo hydroxide on the NF was placed downstream, and sodium hypophosphite monohydrate (NaH₂PO₂), as a phosphorous precursor, was placed upstream of the tube furnace. Subsequently, the sample was annealed at 500 °C for 2 h at a ramping rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ under an Ar atmosphere to obtain the final RuP₂/Ni₅P₄/NiMoO₄ on the NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform coverage of small nanograins with numerous interfaces covering the entire nickel foam for the 80 mM RuCl3 heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The introduction of RuCl3 through drop-casting followed by phosphorization generated a substantial number of small nanograins with numerous interfaces, which cover the entire NF (Fig. 1d–h and Figs. S1d–r).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS confirms presence of Ru, Mo, Ni, P, and O with Ru atomic percentage of 1.02 wt% in the 80 mM RuCl3 heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) combined with scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed the presence of Ru, Mo, Ni, P, and O in all Ru-doped heterostructure samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES measurements show Ru mass percentage of 1.02 wt% and mass loading of 61 μg cm⁻² for the 80 mM RuCl3 heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma – optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) measurements indicated that the mass percentage of Ru in the heterostructure samples was calculated to be 0.25%, 0.86%, 1.02%, 1.29%, and 2.22% for RuCl3 concentrations of 10, 40, 80, 120, and 160 mM, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks for RuP2 (PDF# 00-034-0333), Ni5P4 (PDF# 01-076-4287), NiMoO4 (PDF# 01-079-7552), MoO2 (PDF# 00-002-0422), and Ni (111, 200, 220) confirming formation of 3D heterostructures composed of three distinct phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the RuP2/Ni5P4/NiMoO4 sample, peaks corresponding to RuP2 peaks (PDF# 00.034.0333) were observed alongside new peaks, indicating the formation of 3D heterostructures composed of three distinct phases of RuP2, Ni5P4, and NiMoO4 (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Mo 3d core level spectra show peaks at 234.1 eV (Mo6+ 3d3/2) and 231.4 eV (Mo4+ 3d3/2) for Ni5P4/NiMoO4, red-shifted by 0.4 and 0.6 eV after Ru incorporation; Ni 2p peaks at 856.4 eV (2p3/2) and 874.6 eV (2p1/2) with Ni-P alloy peak at 854.5 eV red-shifted by 0.8 eV; P 2p peaks at 129.7 eV (2p3/2) and 130.3 eV (2p1/2) red-shifted by 0.4 eV after Ru doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, the XPS Mo 3d core level spectra for the Ni5P4/NiMoO4 sample displayed two major peaks at 234.1 eV for Mo6+ 3d3/2 and 231.4 eV for Mo4+ 3d3/2... After the introduction of Ru... these peaks are red-shifted by 0.4 and 0.6 eV... The Ni 2p core level spectra... revealed two principal peaks at 856.4 (Ni 2p3/2) and 874.6 eV (Ni 2p1/2)... the Ni–P alloy peak, originally at 854.5 eV, underwent a red shift of 0.8 eV... In the P 2p core level spectra... two primary peaks were observed at 129.7 eV (2p3/2) and 130.3 eV (P 2p1/2)... Upon doping with Ru, a red shift of 0.4 eV was observed for the P 2p3/2 peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanometer-sized clusters with uniform elemental distribution of Ru, Mo, Ni, and P throughout the heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification TEM image showed nanometer-sized clusters (Fig. 2d). The corresponding EDS elemental images demonstrated that Ru, Mo, Ni, and P were uniformly distributed throughout the RuP2/Ni5P4/NiMoO4 sample (Fig. 2e–h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals d-spacings of 0.58 nm for Ni5P4 (100) plane, 0.16 nm for RuP2 (310) plane, and 0.19 nm for RuP2 (121) plane with sharp phase segregation between RuP2 and Ni5P4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image... reveals well-defined crystal structures for the Ni5P4 and RuP2 phases... d-spacings of 0.58 nm for the Ni5P4 (100) plane, 0.16 nm for the RuP2 (310) plane, as well as 0.19 nm for the RuP2 (121) plane (Fig. 2i–k).

nodes.characterization_summary: The electrochemical double layer capacitance (Cdl) was calculated as 98.1 mF cm⁻², significantly higher than Pt/C (31.7 mF cm⁻²), RuO2 (37.4 mF cm⁻²), and bare NF (9.9 mF cm⁻²), demonstrating abundance of catalytically active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) was used to estimate the electrochemical double layer capacitance (Cdl). The Cdl of RuP2/Ni5P4/NiMoO4 stands out with a 98.1 mF cm⁻². This was significantly higher than that of Pt/C (31.7 mF cm⁻²), RuO2 (37.4 mF cm⁻²), and bare NF (9.9 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows Raman peaks at 477 cm⁻¹ (Eg, δ(Ni-O)) and 557 cm⁻¹ (A1g, υ(Ni-O)) above 0.4 V vs Hg/HgO confirming NiOOH formation as active species during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectroscopy was conducted... upon exceeding 0.4 V, two new Raman peaks emerged at 477 cm⁻¹ and 557 cm⁻¹. These are identified as the Eg (δ(Ni-O)) and A1g (υ(Ni-O)) modes associated with NiOOH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS reveals charge-transfer resistances (Rct) of 0.25 Ω for HER and 0.39 Ω for OER, lower than Pt/C (0.66 Ω for HER) and RuO2 (0.43 Ω for OER).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) revealed that RuP2/Ni5P4/NiMoO4 has significantly low charge-transfer resistances (Rct) of 0.25 and 0.39 Ω for HER and OER, respectively.
